claim: Primary external evaluation used the corrected locked MedSeg CT preprocessing pathway.
reason: Corrected Notebook-09 evaluation used the frozen CT normalization pathway and was preserved separately from the invalid initial preprocessing run.

claim: Supervised, confidence-only EMA, and agreement-filtered EMA models were evaluated without target-guided retraining.
reason: Target evaluation occurred only after the Notebook-08 protocol freeze.

claim: The semantic real-text branch showed a repeatable source-side descriptive benefit relative to controls.
reason: The semantic branch showed descriptive improvement but was not established as a formally significant universal gain.

claim: The source-derived p80 uncertainty gate provides approximately 80% external-target coverage.
reason: Observed MedSeg coverage was only a few percent, showing substantial source-to-target uncertainty-distribution shift.

claim: Lower uncertainty preferentially selected lower-error external cases at matched reporting coverage.
reason: Matched-coverage selective-risk reductions were positive on average for all three evaluated methods.

claim: Prediction uncertainty was positively associated with lesion-extent error.
reason: Uncertainty-versus-extent-error Spearman correlations were positive across all seeds and methods.

claim: The strict sentence-ID reporting pathway prevents the language model from generating protected numerical lesion-extent values.
reason: Protected numerical values were never supplied to or generated by Qwen in the strict arm; Python performed the final rendering.

claim: Controlled free-text reporting achieved 896/900 directly accepted outputs with 100% protected-number integrity after validator-only software corrections.
reason: The same frozen raw Qwen outputs were revalidated without new generation, prompt changes, or target information.

claim: All three reporting pathways produced 900/900 safe deliverable outputs after deterministic fallback.
reason: Rejected strict/free-text outputs were replaced by the validated deterministic evidence-grounded report.

claim: Synthetic noise, blur, and resolution experiments establish robustness to real-world clinical acquisition variation.
reason: Notebook-12B perturbations are synthetic stress tests only.

claim: EViCT measures physical lesion area in mm² or lesion volume in cm³.
reason: Verified physical geometry / volumetric metadata are not available for the locked external evaluation.

claim: MedSeg external results represent independent patient-level volumetric performance.
reason: The evaluation unit is a selected 2D image; verified patient grouping is unavailable.

claim: EViCT demonstrates superior clinical report quality according to independent expert readers.
reason: No independent qualified reader study was performed.

claim: The complete originally planned 25%, 50%, and 100% low-label experiment grid was executed.
reason: The completed reduced-compute study centers on b050; b025 was explicitly deferred due to compute budget.

claim: Agreement-filtered EMA is universally the best uncertainty estimator across every reliability metric.
reason: Matched-coverage reliability varied by method and seed; confidence-only EMA showed stronger selective segmentation risk behavior in several analyses.

claim: The external uncertainty findings support a useful but modest selective reliability signal.
reason: Matched-coverage risk and measurement-error analyses showed directionally favorable selection while effect magnitude varied by method and seed.
